classification.difficultyReason: Translate snug packing into a cylinder radius and shared box length, calculate both closed-box surface areas, and subtract to interpret the cardboard saving.

content.prompt:
Circular cracker biscuits of diameter $4\text{ cm}$ are packed in a cardboard box of length $20\text{ cm}$.
How much cardboard would be saved if the biscuits were packed into a cylindrical box instead?
The rectangular box has a $4\text{ cm}\times4\text{ cm}$ cross-section. Both boxes are closed and fit the biscuits snugly. Ignore flaps and overlaps. Give your answer to the nearest square centimetre.

spec.description: Oblique square-cross-section biscuit carton with an open display flap and a circular biscuit inscribed in its end. Decorative blue fill is omitted. The diagram displays the contents; the comparison concerns closed boxes.
spec.mathematics: A diameter-4 cm circle fits snugly in a 4 cm square; package length is 20 cm. The centre and a diameter arrow are retained.

answer.worked:
The biscuit radius is $r=2\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}
A_{\text{rectangular box}}&=2(4\times4)+4(4\times20)\\
A_{\text{rectangular box}}&=352\text{ cm}^2\\
A_{\text{cylindrical box}}&=2\pi(2)^2+2\pi(2)(20)\\
A_{\text{cylindrical box}}&=88\pi\text{ cm}^2\\
A_{\text{saved}}&=352-88\pi\\
A_{\text{saved}}&\approx76\text{ cm}^2
\end{align*}$$
